newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mostly weaker.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mostly weaker.

text.p: Med oil products were mostly weaker on Monday, traders said

Gasoline eased with energy futures amid adequate supplies and thin demand for both premium unleaded and lower octane grades, traders said. Premium unleaded cargoes added a further $2-3 to Friday's $8 a tonne losses to talk around $227/$230 cif.
Naphtha prices were soft although traders said the market was better balanced with few surplus prompt cargoes available and buying interest thin.
"End-users are pretty well supplied and there is little sign of trader pricing activity," a traders said.
"We are well supplied and I don't seen any need for us to buy from the spot market at the moment," a trader for an Italian petrochemicals company said.
However, he said that while his requirements for term contracts were mostly covered any top-up needs would probably be covered with cheaper Russian oil.
"Formula calculations are making Algerian cargoes expensive to work unless you want 50-60kt, this is giving Russian material the edge," he added.
Gas oil slipped $2, pushed lower by Dec IPE, which finished at $218.75 a tonne.
Demand for low sulphur diesel was moribund but traders reported offers of 0.2 percent sulphur heating oil at cif quotes high +$1 with Russian rumoured offered at cif quotes high +$5.
Cracked fuel oil markets were quiet, supported by strong Lebanese demand and continued steady interest from Italy.
Traders said they were watching an arbitrage opening to the U.S. for Russian although vessels had yet to be fixed.

A winter export tariff on Russian fuel oil was still in discussion in Moscow on Monday, and a Moscow-based consultant said the various ministries would make their recommendations by December 1. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 8145
